claims.text: Under ambient-pressure solidification, Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 undergoes multistep crystallization.
Under ambient-pressure solidification, Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 forms extensive primary non-eutectic crystalline phases.
A pressure of several GPa can be applied as a processing intervention to a high-entropy alloy.
Applying several GPa specifically during rapid cooling of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 is a suitable processing route.
High pressure increases the nucleation barrier for crystalline phases in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
High pressure during cooling retards atomic mobility in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Pressure-retarded atomic mobility inhibits the atomic rearrangement required for crystallization.
Suppressing crystalline nucleation and atomic rearrangement stabilizes the amorphous phase.
Pressure treatment during quenching will suppress primary non-eutectic crystallization in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
The pressure intervention will suppress primary crystallite formation even during slower cooling or mild reheating.
The pressure intervention will broaden the supercooled-liquid region.
Relative to ambient-pressure processing, pressure-assisted quenching will increase the amorphous-phase volume fraction.
Relative to ambient-pressure processing, pressure-assisted quenching will increase the crystallization-onset temperature during reheating.
The beneficial effect requires a cooling rate above the alloy's critical cooling rate.
The pressure must be maintained during the critical nucleation period for the intervention to be effective.
If cooling falls below the critical rate or pressure is not sustained, crystallization may dominate.
Reheating below the crystallization-onset temperature is an applicable boundary for assessing retained amorphous stability.
